.WHAT HAS CHANGED...

No significant changes.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 126 PM EDT Friday...

1. A couple showers today before dry weather tomorrow. 

2. Periods of rain late Sunday into Monday. 

3. Near seasonable temperatures with a chance for showers and 
thunderstorms mid week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 126 PM EDT Friday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: A weak shortwave will pass through the region 
from northwest to southeast this afternoon and evening, but the 
strongest dynamics will mostly be to the south. An associated 
area of showers and embedded thunderstorms has developed west of
Ottawa and those will move southeast into southwestern St. 
Lawrence County. A briefly stronger storm is possible there. The
storms should mostly pass south of Rutland County, though a 
brief isolated shower is possible there. Pea sized hail and 
gusty winds are possible in the strongest storm in St. Lawrence 
County. After that, a gorgeous opener to the weekend will occur 
on Saturday with seasonably cool temperatures and low humidity.

KEY MESSAGE 2: A double barrel low will move into the region 
late Sunday into Sunday night, bringing rounds of rain. The 
primary low will track well north of the St. Lawrence, while the
secondary low will try to spin up off the coast of southern New
England, but they will both remain on the weaker side. The Euro
ensembles generally bring the heavier rain associated with the 
southern low farther north and into the region, while the GEFS 
members generally split the region between the areas of low 
pressure and bring lighter precip. Overall, combined 
EPS/GEFS/CMCE probabilities of receiving more than a half inch 
are between 40-70 percent, and the probabilities of seeing more 
than an inch are less than 10 percent. Some convective 
enhancement is possible across southern areas, but no flooding 
is expected. Very weak lapse rates, a notable inversion and 
unfavorable timing should prevent much of a severe threat, 
though a trend north in storm track could still produce 
something, so the threat will continue to be watched. A few 
lingering showers are possible on Monday as a weak shortwave 
moves through under broad cyclonic flow.

KEY MESSAGE 3: High pressure and calm weather embedded in broad
cyclonic flow will continue through Tuesday as temperatures 
slowly rise to near or just above seasonable levels. Highs will 
be in the upper 70s to low 80s heading into the mid week. 
Humidity will remain on the lower side Tuesday, but as flow 
shift slightly to the southwest by late Tuesday into Wednesday, 
some moisture advection is expected by mid week. The next 
weather maker will arrive by Wednesday into Thursday with a cold
frontal passage. Models are in pretty good agreement for rain 
and possible thunder chances Wednesday afternoon for the higher 
terrain and into late Wednesday for most locations, however, how
long showers linger remains in question. The GFS is the fastest
of the model suite clearing the area of precipitation by 
Thursday afternoon. The Euro and Canadian favor a longer system,
with more positive tilting to the trough axis, and 
precipitation persisting through the day Thursday. Regardless, 
pwats look to increase to around an inch, though where the best 
forcing sets up will determine how much of the precipitable 
water is realized. Temperatures mid to late week will slowly 
decrease from the low 80s to the upper 70s, along with a drying 
surface with dewpoints sinking back down to the low 50s.

&&

.AVIATION /00Z SATURDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...
Through 00Z Sunday...Calm and variable winds will continue as 
high pressure nudges in from the northwest. Outside of any 
variable winds, northerly flow aloft will prevail through the 
TAF period. Clouds are clearing after sunset with some patchy 
fog possible in the climatologically favored terminals. Winds 
likely will decouple at most sites and have trended favored 
sites towards prevailing fog tonight with 3SM BR to start. 
Highest confidence in prevailing fog is at SLK/MPV, though 
clearing skies and calmer winds bodes some confidence, albeit 
lower than SLK/MPV, for intermittent, potentially closer to 
sunrise, fog at EFK/RUT. Winds will need to be watched after 
sunset for any further calming trends that will increase or 
decrease fog chances, especially with any light easterly flow 
for BTV. Fog will lift between 12-13Z where it develops. Winds 
will become prevailing from the north-northwest after sunrise 
tomorrow with mostly clear skies.
